timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: AI security — is that just regular security for AI?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: No. LLMs have unique attack vectors. Prompt injection, data poisoning, model theft. Traditional security doesn't cover these.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Same concept, different target. You craft input that makes the AI ignore its instructions and do what you want instead.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: That's terrifying. What about training data poisoning?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Attackers corrupt the training data to make the model produce biased or malicious outputs. Like teaching a kid with a corrupted textbook.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: It's governance for AI. Track which models exist, who uses them, what data they access, and ensure compliance.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: They detect and block prompt injection attacks against LLMs. Microsoft's answer to the OWASP LLM Top 10.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: It maps real-world AI attacks to tactics and techniques. Like ATT&CK but specifically for AI and ML systems.
